gloss: to organize; to form; to compose (a group)

definitions.gloss: to organize; to form; to compose; to put together
definitions.explanation: To assemble people, units, or elements into an organized group or structure. Used for forming teams, military units, train configurations, budgets, and other organized arrangements.

examples.japanese: チームを{編成|へんせい}する。
{予算|よさん}を{編成|へんせい}する{作業|さぎょう}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The work of putting together the budget has begun.

examples.japanese: {専門家|せんもんか}を{集|あつ}めて{調査|ちょうさ}{委員会|いいんかい}を{編成|へんせい}した。
examples.english: They gathered experts and formed an investigation committee.

notes:
Emphasizes the deliberate assembly and arrangement of components into an organized whole. The resulting group has structure and purpose, not just a random collection.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チームを{編成|へんせい}する: to form a team
- {予算|よさん}を{編成|へんせい}する: to draw up a budget
- {部隊|ぶたい}を{編成|へんせい}する: to organize a military unit
- {番組|ばんぐみ}{編成|へんせい}: program scheduling (TV/radio)
- {列車|れっしゃ}{編成|へんせい}: train composition/formation
- {編成|へんせい}{替|が}え: reorganization

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {組織|そしき}する: to organize — broader, focuses on creating an organizational structure
- {結成|けっせい}する: to form / to establish — for newly creating a group, party, or alliance
- {構成|こうせい}する: to compose / to make up — focuses on what elements something consists of

REGISTER:
Formal. Standard in administrative, military, and media contexts. In casual speech, people more often say チームを{作|つく}る or グループを{組|く}む.
